title: Completed open exchange agrees with the actual constant-coefficient strict mate
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be the Noetherian adic datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with finite perfect quotients $P_n=A/I^n$, completed ring sheaves $A_V=\lim_n(P_n)_V$, and strict quotient towers. Let $(j:U\hookrightarrow T,j':U'\hookrightarrow T',u:T'\to T,v:U'\to U)$ be a cartesian open square, with $j$ quasi-compact [def-cbc-open-immersion-square, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use exact localized ringed extension by zero [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_U))$ be intrinsically derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Assume $j_!K$ is complete and identify $(j_!K)_\bullet\cong J_jK_\bullet$ by the canonical open-tensor quotient comparisons.
Let $r_V$ be restriction along $\underline A_V\to A_V$ and use the canonical finite-reduction and derived-limit identifications, including completion units, of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Put $M=r_UK_\bullet$ and use the constant-ring operations $G_u,G_v,J_j,J_{j'}$ of [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Set $N=G_uJ_jM$ and $N'=J_{j'}G_vM$. Let $Q=Lu^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}(j_!K)_\bullet$ and $Q'=J_{j'}Lv^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$, using the derived strict-tower pullback of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].
Let $\omega_K$ be the actual strict finite open exchange of [lem-cbc-completed-ring-strict-finite-exchange], with source transported by the assumed quotient identification. Thus the finite open exchanges, whose inverses are the transposes of the pulled-back open units, give the specified natural isomorphism $\omega_K:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Q'$ in the derived category of strict $A_{T'}$-towers. This construction uses the finite unit maps on strict representatives with their quotient transitions [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars]. Under the specified scalar and finite-reduction comparisons $a:r_{T'}Q\simeq N$, $b:r_{T'}Q'\simeq N'$, it satisfies
$$b\circ r_{T'}(\omega_K)=\beta_{j,u,M}\circ a,$$
where $\beta$ is the constant-$A$ strict open unit-mate of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. This is an equality of strict-tower derived morphisms before evaluation.
Let $\beta_K^{\mathrm{comp}}:Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\to j'_!Lv^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ be the canonical completed comparison induced by these finite exchanges and the extension/limit comparison [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison]. Write $L_V$ for constant-$A$ total derived inverse limit and $\lambda_{j'}:j'_!L_{U'}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{T'}J_{j'}$ for the specified normalized comparison of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Under the canonical coefficient and finite-reduction endpoint identifications, the ordered comparison satisfies
$$r_{T'}(\beta_K^{\mathrm{comp}})=\lambda_{j'}^{-1}\circ L_{T'}(\beta_{j,u,M}).$$
All assertions are natural in $K$; evaluation of the already specified $\omega_K$ gives the finite open exchange at each $n$. No etale-origin witnesses, common lower bound, or faithfulness of derived evaluation is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-completed-ring-strict-finite-exchange] with $X=T$, $X'=T'$, $g=u$, $g_U=v$. Precompose its source with the assumed canonical identification $(j_!K)_\bullet\simeq J_jK_\bullet$. This gives the specified isomorphism $\omega_K:Q\simeq Q'$ together with its inverse on simultaneous strict diagram representatives. The cited assertion supplies completed-ring linearity, all quotient-transition squares, and the inverse's open-unit transpose normalization. Thus this step selects the actual strict map, rather than selecting finite derived arrows and attempting to lift them. No completeness condition is needed for this application; the completeness assumptions will type the completed endpoints.

proof.text: Fix the scalar and finite-reduction endpoint comparisons $a,b$ in the question using [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Restriction of scalars keeps the underlying abelian sheaves and maps [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. It commutes with open extension: on its presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] both orders give the identical direct sum of the same sections with the restricted action; [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] sheafifies precisely that abelian presheaf. The extension adjunction unit is the same section on an object over the open, by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Consequently the scalar/open comparison preserves this unit; this is the isomorphism $e$ of [lem-cbc-ringed-open-scalar-limit-coherence], which identifies the units and counits of the two open-extension adjunctions on sheaves, complexes and derived strict towers. The finite-reduction comparisons commute with quotient transitions by the completion-equivalence lemma, so $a,b$ compare strict diagrams, with these unit identifications, before passing to their derived categories. On strict flat representatives the finite tensor comparisons reassociate tensor factors and send a local pure tensor to the same tensor. Applying an open unit changes only its section by the identity on the open. Thus these comparisons intertwine the pulled-back unit and the inverse-image square compositor; the equality persists after deriving.

proof.text: Write $H=G_vM$, and denote the constant-coefficient open unit by $e_M:M\to G_jJ_jM$. Let $t_H:H\to G_{j'}N$ be $G_v(e_M)$ followed by the canonical inverse-image square identification. By [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], $\beta_{j,u,M}^{-1}$ is the $J_{j'}\dashv G_{j'}$ adjunct of $t_H$. Compute the restricted inverse from Step 1 using Step 2. Its unit is $e_M$, its square comparison is the same inverse-image comparison, and its transpose is therefore exactly $t_H$. This calculation is valid for strict diagram topoi by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. By the mate formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], on representatives its adjunct is the explicit composite $J_{j'}H\xrightarrow{J_{j'}t_H}J_{j'}G_{j'}N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon'_N}N$. The scalar compatibility of the finite units, counits and transitions is [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars]. Hence the restricted inverse and the constant inverse are the same strict diagram map, with source and target compared by $b$ and $a$.

proof.text: Localize the strict representative equality of Step 3 at tower quasi-isomorphisms. The uniqueness and composition clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] identify the descended maps, including the comparisons of representatives. They give $a\,r_{T'}(\omega_K^{-1})\,b^{-1}=\beta_{j,u,M}^{-1}$ in the derived category of constant-$A$ strict towers. Invert this equality and multiply on the right by $a$ to obtain $b\,r_{T'}(\omega_K)=\beta_{j,u,M}a$. This argument descends equality of strict maps; it never infers equality from equality of their derived evaluations.

proof.text: The open $j'$ is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], applied to the given cartesian square and the assumed quasi-compact $j$. Its constant-$A$ ringed extension by zero is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] and preserves countable products with the canonical projection comparison by [lem-cbc-ringed-open-extension-products]. Countable products in both constant-$A$ module-sheaf categories are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] to this exact functor. At $H=G_vM$ it supplies precisely the specified normalized isomorphism $\lambda_{j',H}:j'_!L_{U'}H\simeq L_{T'}J_{j'}H=L_{T'}N'$.

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] to identify the completed source with the completed-ring derived limit of $Q$ and the completed pullback on $U'$ with the limit of $Lv^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$. The scalar comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identify these limits and their quotient-tower completion units with the constant-coefficient limits. Write $\lambda_{r}$ for the normalized scalar/limit comparison $r\,R\lim\xrightarrow{\sim}L\,r$ of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] for the exact, product-preserving functor $r$ (identity product comparison on underlying abelian sheaves). The source comparison is therefore $L_{T'}(a)\circ\lambda_{r_{T'},Q}$. For the target apply [lem-cbc-ringed-open-scalar-limit-coherence] to the quasi-compact open $j'$ of Step 5, the ring map $\underline A_{T'}\to A_{T'}$ and $M'=Lv^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$: its natural isomorphism $e:r_{T'}J_{j'}\simeq J_{j'}r_{U'}$ identifies the open units, and its displayed equation $L_{T'}(e_{M'})\lambda_{r_{T'},J_{j'}M'}r_{T'}(\lambda^{\mathrm{comp}}_{j',M'})=\lambda_{j',r_{U'}M'}\,j'_!(\lambda_{r_{U'},M'})\,e_{R\lim M'}$ rewrites the scalar restriction of the completed extension/limit comparison $\lambda^{\mathrm{comp}}_{j'}$ used in [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] as the constant-$A$ comparison $\lambda_{j'}$. Composing with $j'_!L_{U'}$ of the $U'$-level comparison $r_{U'}M'\simeq G_vM$ (whose $J_{j'}$-image after $e$ is $b$) and naturality of $\lambda_{j'}$ gives the target endpoint $r(j'_!Lv^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K)\simeq j'_!L_{U'}H$, and shows that $r_{T'}(\lambda^{\mathrm{comp},-1}_{j'})$ becomes $\lambda_{j',H}^{-1}\circ L_{T'}(b)$ under these endpoint identifications. The normalized $\lambda$ of Step 5 is the comparison from preserving ordinary inverse limit and resolving the image tower, as stated in [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Its strict-augmentation clause preserves the quotient-tower completion maps. These facts fix the endpoint identifications with their units, without choosing an arbitrary isomorphism between the limits.

proof.text:
By the definition of the canonical map in [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison], first take derived limit of the finite open exchange and then apply the inverse extension/limit comparison. Here those finite arrows are the actual simultaneous strict map $\omega_K$ of Step 1. Functoriality of derived inverse limit [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality], naturality of $\lambda_r$ applied to $\omega_K$, and the endpoint comparisons of Step 6 (the scalar/open limit square of [lem-cbc-ringed-open-scalar-limit-coherence] for the final factor) therefore express the restricted completed map, in the stated endpoints, as the ordered composite
$$\lambda_{j',H}^{-1}\circ L_{T'}(b)\circ L_{T'}(r_{T'}\omega_K)\circ L_{T'}(a)^{-1}.$$
Apply $L_{T'}$ to the strict-derived equality in Step 4. The middle three factors become $L_{T'}(\beta_{j,u,M})$. Thus the ordered composite is exactly $\lambda_{j'}^{-1}\circ L_{T'}(\beta_{j,u,M})$, as required.

proof.text: All maps used above are natural in $K$: Step 1 supplies a natural strict isomorphism, the scalar/reduction comparisons are natural, the constant open mate is natural, and $\lambda$ is a natural transformation. Composing their naturality squares proves naturality of the two displayed equalities. Applying evaluation to the already constructed $\omega_K$ recovers the specified finite open exchange by [lem-cbc-completed-ring-strict-finite-exchange]. No part of Steps 1--7 uses etale-origin data or boundedness: the finite strict assertion is unbounded, and the exact-product comparison applies to arbitrary strict tower complexes.
